newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 14.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Monday:
- Former Irish prime minister Charles Haughey is facing the possibility of a jail sentence regardless of his evidence to the Dunnes Payments Tribunal on Tuesday.
- The British government has resumed contact with Sinn Fein about a new IRA ceasefire.
- A motorcycle enthusiast was killed in front of a crowd of 15,000 people in one of Ireland's biggest road races on Sunday.
- Ireland's domestic businesses need to be more competitive if they are to survive in the single European currency, two new research papers from Trinity College Dublin suggest.
- Cologne-based Oppenheim Jun & Cie has bought control of the small Dublin investment management firm Montgomery Govett.
- The British government has resumed contact with Sinn Fein in a further attempt to clarify the terms for republican involvement in all-party talks on the future of Northern Ireland.

- The government faces a crucial decision before publication of the McCracken tribunal report after the tribunal's legal team lodged an appeal against the refusal of a Cayman Islands court to permit collection of evidence.
- Fifteen people were left homeless as freak floods caused an estimated one million punts in damage in north Mayo over the weekend.
- The first moves toward shaping a November budget, including reductions in the two tax rates, will be undertaken tomorrow when ministers hold a day-long cabinet meeting.

- A former IRA southern commander and the IRA's head of intelligence in Munster are among five people being held by police for questioning in Limerick in connection with the investigation into the murder of detective Jerry McCabe.

- Senior Fianna Fail sources dismissed reports of a rift with the Progressive Democrats over a row about opening up Fianna Fail constituency accounts relating to Charles Haughey's Dublin electoral base.
